input.question: In which significant event was Partially-fluorinated silane bonding agent involved?

documents.text: As the sun set over the bustling port of Chittagong, Bangladesh, the air was thick with the smell of saltwater, grease, and the acrid tang of welding torches. The ship breaking yards, a labyrinthine complex of rusting hulls and scavenged machinery, hummed with activity. It was here, amidst the chaos, that Amir Khan, a grizzled shipbreaker, had spent the better part of his life dismantling the world's discarded vessels. Amir's latest project, the hulking cargo ship, "Sea Dragon," loomed before him, its steel plates scarred and battered from years of service. As he surveyed the ship's weathered decks, his mind turned to the peculiar request from the yard's owner, Mr. Rahman. The old man had been insistent that Amir use a new, experimental bonding agent on the ship's hull – something called "FluoroSil" – to ensure the vessel's fragile components remained intact during the dismantling process. Amir had raised an eyebrow at the unusual request, but Mr. Rahman's connections with the mysterious "Syndicate of Shipwrights" had piqued his curiosity. The Syndicate, rumored to be a secretive organization of shipbuilders and salvagers, was said to possess knowledge passed down through generations of maritime craftsmen. If they recommended FluoroSil, Amir was willing to give it a try. As he mixed the bonding agent with a practiced hand, Amir noticed the unusual sheen it imparted to the ship's metal. The FluoroSil seemed to bond with the steel on a molecular level, creating an almost imperceptible glow that danced across the surface. It was as if the very essence of the ship was being awakened, its metal heart beating in time with the rhythm of the breaking yard. The days that followed were a blur of sweat, toil, and the constant din of machinery. Amir and his team worked tirelessly to disassemble the Sea Dragon, FluoroSil proving to be a game-changer in their efforts. The bonding agent allowed them to extract delicate components with ease, as if the ship itself was surrendering its secrets to the breakers. It wasn't until the night of the full moon, when the yard was bathed in an otherworldly glow, that Amir began to suspect the true extent of FluoroSil's involvement in the ship breaking process.

accepted_answers: dismantling of the cargo ship "Sea Dragon"
